learningObjectives: Select and justify activities in a business scenario.
Select and justify activity structure in a business scenario.
Select and justify declare onchange rules in a business scenario.
reviewScope: Official topic comparison and original-question editorial review; not vendor endorsement.

elements.description: Activities run ordered steps for procedural processing. Prefer a suitable out-of-the-box automation, Data Transform or specialized rule before custom activity code. Activities increase maintenance cost; a requirement for an activity should be explicit rather than a default for every data update.

elements.text: Worked example: Use a Data Transform for a simple address mapping. Use an appropriate standard automation for a supported case action; justify any custom activity with a missing specialized mechanism.

elements.description: An activity step specifies a method, parameters and optional step page. The step page supplies the data context; Pages & Classes declares page/class references. Preconditions, loops and transitions control execution. Call returns to the caller; Branch transfers execution without returning to subsequent caller steps.

elements.text: Worked example: An activity loops through embedded Item pages, setting the step page to the current item. A Call to validation returns for later processing; a Branch is appropriate only when the caller must not resume.

elements.description: Declare OnChange watches configured property changes and can execute activities or suspend work through a business-exception condition. Its trigger is a change, unlike a Declare Expression's derived-value dependency. Keep frequently triggered processing small and guard it with suitable conditions.

elements.text: Worked example: When a RiskScore changes above a threshold, an OnChange condition triggers the appropriate investigation activity. Test repeated changes and ensure the activity does not create an unintended change loop.

elements.title: Training environment checklist
items: Implement the worked example in a training application; use synthetic data.
Test the expected path and at least one failure or boundary condition.
Explain why the alternative mechanism would not meet the requirement.
Revisit incorrect answers in Smart Review rather than memorizing option positions.

elements.text: These notes target the '25 exam. Shared Academy pages may show newer labels with '25 applicability; verify screens in your training environment.

examPitfalls.title: Activity by default
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Use custom activities for every mapping and calculation.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Evaluate specialized and declarative rules first.

examPitfalls.title: Call versus Branch
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Both continue at the next caller step.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Call returns; Branch does not resume the caller sequence.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A requirement only copies and maps fields between pages. Which mechanism should be evaluated before a custom activity?

options.text: A new Java activity for every property

practiceQuiz.rationale: Data Transforms specialize in data manipulation and avoid unnecessary procedural maintenance.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A standard case automation already satisfies a requirement. Which design choice is preferred?

options.text: Hard-code it into a portal label
Use the supported automation instead of duplicating it in custom code
Rewrite all of its behavior in Java

practiceQuiz.rationale: Reusing supported automation reduces custom behavior to maintain and upgrade.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An activity step must operate on an embedded item page. Which field sets that context?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The step page determines the page against which the method runs. Declare its page/class context appropriately.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An activity invokes another activity and must continue with its next step afterward. Which instruction fits?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Call returns control to the caller; Branch transfers processing without continuing the caller's subsequent sequence.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are part of an activity step's execution definition?

options.text: A step page when a different data context is required

practiceQuiz.rationale: Methods, parameters and page context define the procedural operation and where it acts.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A property change should trigger an activity when a business condition becomes true. Which rule fits?

options.text: A Field Value used only as a label

practiceQuiz.rationale: Declare OnChange monitors property changes and invokes conditional processing.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why should a frequently changing watched property be considered carefully?

options.text: The triggered activity can add repeated processing cost
OnChange never executes more than once
It automatically caches every connector response

practiceQuiz.rationale: Frequent triggers can cause significant overhead. Scope and guard the processing appropriately.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A total should stay derived from component amounts without an action side effect. Which rule better matches than OnChange activity code?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A derived value is a declarative dependency. OnChange is for actions tied to change, not a default replacement for expressions.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.
